A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same F5-TTS research. All 18 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original F5-TTS benchmark results, human evaluations, architecture and sampling ablations, and hard-sentence tests.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds vocoder, solver, text-formatting, and training-data-scale experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed DiT/ConvNeXt architecture, text padding, flow-matching objective, duration estimation, CFG, and Sway Sampling remain unchanged. Additional solver and vocoder options are evaluated as ablations; the default Euler/Vocos pipeline is retained.

E1.justification: Appendix B.7 adds training on multi-speaker LibriTTS (585 hours) and single-speaker LJSpeech (24 hours), with additional LJSpeech in-set evaluation. Appendix B.6 also adds a controlled uncapitalized, punctuation-free input scenario. These extend the original multilingual and Mandarin training coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds the 361M-parameter USLM comparator, evaluated using its official LibriTTS-trained checkpoint in Table 9. Comparator membership in the main benchmark tables and ELLA-V hard-sentence comparison remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V3 introduces UTMOS naturalness measurement, additional HuBERT-based WER measurement, punctuation/capitalization removal, and Heun-3/BigVGAN evaluation configurations. The new training-scale experiments evaluate checkpoints from 100K to 600K updates and specify 1,000 LJSpeech in-set test examples. The original main training and evaluation settings remain.

E4.justification: Appendices B.6–B.7 add analyses of vocoder dependence, sensitivity to text formatting and ASR choice, and training behavior across smaller datasets. The solver ablation adds Heun-3, while UTMOS extends the sampling analysis to objective naturalness. Existing architecture, input-condition, leak-and-override, and hard-sentence analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over three random generation seeds, and v3 applies that practice to its new training-scale results. Neither introduces confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty estimates. Newly disclosed listener counts do not establish increased repetition or changed uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Main benchmark scores remain unchanged, but v3 adds UTMOS results, Heun-3 rows, and Tables 8–9 covering vocoders, non-PC inputs, and smaller training datasets. For example, the original 32-NFE Vocos WER of 2.42 on LibriSpeech-PC is retained alongside a new BigVGAN result of 2.11. V1's base-model ground-truth-duration WER results of 1.74/1.53 are omitted.

T1.justification: Sections 2–3 retain the same flow-matching derivations, CFG formulation, text-padding definition, and Sway Sampling equation and coefficient range. Notation is tidied, but no mathematical assumption, derivation, proposition, or proof is substantively changed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: simple non-autoregressive TTS, ConvNeXt text refinement, transferable inference-time Sway Sampling, robust zero-shot synthesis, and an RTF of 0.15. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V3 adds explicit limitations concerning long mel-spectrogram representations and insufficient fine-grained paralinguistic control. It also interprets the new small-dataset experiments as evidence of training stability and attributes F5-TTS's text-only WER improvement to more ASR-friendly output. The central alignment and early-flow explanations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly documents native-listener counts, evaluation rounds, rating scales, instructions, and score aggregation. V3 also identifies RTX 3090 hardware for RTF measurement, provides H100 training-time information for the new experiments, and identifies additional metric implementations. Most architecture, optimizer, preprocessing, and resource-access information was already present.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for A3T, HuBERT, BigVGAN, UTMOS, LibriTTS, and LJSpeech, while dropping the original LibriSpeech and StyleTTS 2 bibliography entries. These are limited attribution and experimental-context changes; positioning relative to E2 TTS and other TTS approaches remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 reorganizes the Section 5.1 argument, trims several explanations, swaps the solver and Sway Sampling appendix subsections, and adds dedicated limitations and subjective-evaluation sections. Citation style and affiliation text also change, while most existing methodological exposition is retained.

P2.justification: The paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, with substantial resizing and relocation of tables and figures. Figures 2–3 receive revised typography and legends while retaining their plotted findings. Tables 5–6 are reordered and expanded, and Tables 8–9 are added.

improvement.justification: V3 improves transparency through human-evaluation details and explicit limitations, and strengthens supporting evidence through solver, vocoder, text-formatting, and training-scale checks. These gains are bounded: headline results remain unchanged, LJSpeech evaluation is in-set, and its WER worsens after 200K updates. Table 1 also loses explicit literature-result markers, although Appendix A retains provenance. Overall, the added evidence and documentation provide a useful but limited quality improvement.
